notes: The stub is already out of your hands and the house is paying the maid for it: the kitchen crisis over Lavinia comes first, then the Major follows Ellingham's pen across to your own turned-out room, where the hairpin forces the second choice. The tallow box is the one quiet clue, and the baize door is the way forward once both are faced.
opening: The tallow stub Lavinia Netherby carried down under her apron is no longer in your box; it is in Major Carrington's pocket, and he fills the servants' hall door with his notebook open. At the long table the cook has Lavinia by the wrist, ash grey down the front of her apron, and the kitchen has gone quiet to watch. Across the passage, drawers scrape in the housekeeper's room, where Mr Ellingham is listing what is taken from you, item by item. Lavinia says it was her that took it, and looks at you.

variants.text: The cook is back at her range and the long table has been wiped where the ash came off Lavinia's apron. Nobody looks at the cook's chair. The Major's boots have gone across the passage to your door.

The long table, the cook's chair pushed back, and Lavinia Netherby held by the wrist at the end nearest the hearth, ash on her apron. Major Carrington stands in the door with his book. Every face in the room is turned carefully elsewhere.
Lavinia's empty pail still stands on the dog-leg turn where she set it down to listen to you. Nobody has moved it. Above, on the landing, Mrs Ormsby has stopped with one hand on the rope rail.

There is no pail on the turn; she kept hold of it the whole time you spoke, her eyes on the door below, and carried it down with her. Above, on the landing, Mrs Ormsby has stopped with one hand on the rope rail.
The candle streak on the wall has a second, fresher mark beside it. On the landing above, Mrs Ormsby has stopped with one hand on the rope rail, not coming down.

Your box is open on the iron bed and the deal desk drawers are out on the floor. Mr Ellingham writes at the desk. On the landing beyond the door Millicent Gresham stands pointing the Major to the second drawer, the one you keep locked.

Your box is open on the iron bed and the deal desk drawers are out on the floor. Mr Ellingham writes at the desk. Millicent Gresham's door across the landing is shut, and stays shut, though the Major has knocked on it twice.

Your box is open on the iron bed, the drawers of the deal desk pulled out and set on the floor in a row. Mr Ellingham sits at your desk with the inventory, pen raised. The old housekeeper's bonnet has been moved off its peg and not put back.

options.detail: 'I sent her up. The stub was mine.'
options.label: 'I sent her up. The stub was mine.'
options.text: You say it to the room, not to him: you sent her for the stub and the ash pan, and it was yours to ask for. The Major turns a page and writes your name below hers, in the same hand. The cook lets go of Lavinia's wrist as if it had gone hot.

options.label: take her into your room, shut the door
options.text: You take Lavinia by the elbow, walk her past the Major and across the passage, and shut the kitchen door on the cook's open mouth. In your room she gets a chair and a clean apron from your box. The kitchen talks of you instead, for the rest of the day.

options.label: say nothing; let the cook finish
options.text: You stand where staff stand and say nothing. The cook finishes. Lavinia is given her notice at the table with the ash still on her apron, and does not look at you again.

options.label: 'Finish your list first, Major.'
options.text: The Major considers you, then the girl, and shuts his book without writing. 'Nobody leaves this floor,' he says, and goes across to Ellingham. The cook keeps hold of the wrist.

options.detail: 'A lady's. I could not say whose.'
options.label: 'A lady's. I could not say whose.'
options.text: Ellingham looks at the jet head of the pin, then at you, and writes 'one hairpin' and nothing after it. On the landing the widow's hand leaves the rail and her step goes away upward.

options.label: 'Mrs Ormsby's, from the study keyhole'
options.text: You name it: Mrs Ormsby's, found at the study keyhole on the stroke of midnight. Ellingham writes it all, the hour included, and the Major turns his head to the landing. Cordelia Ormsby goes to Dr Ashcombe's door without a word and does not come out.

options.label: hand the Major your rounds book
options.text: You say nothing of the pin. You take your rounds book from under the account book and hold it out to the Major before he can find it himself. He takes it as if it had always been his and tells Ellingham to list it last.

options.label: 'Count the rest first, sir.'
options.text: Ellingham sets the pin on the blotter beside his inventory and goes on with the drawers. The Major stays in the door. The pin sits there, black on white, waiting.

actions.label: open the tallow box
actions.text: The box is two stubs short of the count in your account book, and the lid has a grey thumbprint on it that was not there this morning. Someone has been to the box since Lavinia came down.

actions.label: through the baize door to the front
actions.text: You push through the baize into the cold of the front hall, where the snow light is grey through every window and the Major's voice is already carrying from above.

events.text: Major Carrington shuts his notebook, steps out of the servants' hall and crosses to the housekeeper's room, where Mr Ellingham's pen has stopped over something small and black.
From the housekeeper's room, the scrape of a drawer pulled clean out and set down on the boards. Ellingham's voice: 'And this one is locked, Major.'

nudges.text: Mr Ellingham's voice, dry, carrying along the passage: 'The housekeeper, if you please. There is an item here I am not able to name.'
The cook's voice reaches every corner of the lower house: 'Ash on her, plain as print, and nobody to speak for her.'

props.name: your rounds book
props.description: Your small black book of the night's rounds: every door tried, every hour, every name on every landing. The only record in the house of where everyone was.

props.name: the jet hairpin
props.description: A lady's hairpin with a jet head, picked up from the boards at the study keyhole at midnight and kept in your apron pocket since. Now it lies on Ellingham's blotter.
